english.notes:
(i) This offence is intended to cover conduct often referred to as cyber flashing, referring to the act of sending unsolicited sexual images to other persons online or otherwise, for example, via social media or dating apps, but can also over data sharing services such as Bluetooth and Airdrop.
(ii) 'Genitals' refers to male or female sexual organs.
(iii) 'Sending or giving' a photograph or film includes, in particular, sending it to another person by any means, electronically or otherwise, showing it to another person, and placing it for a particular person to find, see section 66A(2). The meaning of sending or giving is intended to be technologically neutral; it does not matter over or through what an image is sent.
(iv) Photographs and film are defined under section 66B, with 66B(5) making clear that the terms include an image, whether made by computer graphics or in any other way, which appears to be a photograph or film; a copy of such an image, photograph or film, and data stored by any means which is capable of conversion into such an image; photograph, or film. The definitions and clarity offered within this section are intended to account for advances in ‘deepfake’ technology that make it easier to create images where it is almost impossible to tell whether they are real or fake and, ensuring the sending or giving of such is captured.
(iv) See also section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003, inserted by the Online Safety Act 2023 and in force from the 31st January 2024, providing for offences relating to the sharing of, or threatening to share, intimate photographs or films.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 66A(6) of this Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
